newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec single-family home sales fell 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec single-family home sales fell 1.0 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior months (numbers in 1,000s).
- Pct----Dec Nov--Rev from Oct--Rev from
-By Region: Pct----Dec Nov--Rev from Oct--Rev from
Total December sales of single-family homes rose 14.6 percent from an annualized rate of 683,000 units a year ago.
In 1,000s: Dec Nov--Rev from Oct--Rev from
Actual Units Sold 51 55 53 54 54
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists had expected December single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 745,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
- Nov-Rev from Oct--Rev from Sept--Rev from
For all of 1996, U.S. single-family home sales rose 13.3 percent to 756,000 units. The department said total sales for the year were the strongest since 1978 when they were 817,000 units.
December's Midwest sales rate of 176,000 units was the strongest since December 1993 when it was 206,000 units, the department said.
The annualized sales rate for September was revised to 779,000 units from 780,000.
The December supply of homes for sale rose to 5.2 months' worth from a revised 5.1 months' worth in November. November was previously reported at 5.2 months.
The inventory of houses for sale at the end of December was 327,000 units, down from a revised 330,000 units in November. November was previously reported at 328,000 units.
The December data was originally scheduled to be released January 31, but the department said it discovered a misprocessed file and delayed the report.
